newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF ATLETICO PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF ATLETICO PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the Atletico Madrid players most likely to play against Real Madrid in Saturday's Spanish league match.

Jose Molina, goalkeeper, age 26. One of the stars of last season's double win after signing from Albacete, Molina's characteristic sorties from the area make the Atletico off-side trap difficult to beat. Came on as a striker and nearly scored on his sole international appearance in a friendly last year.
Santi Denia, defender, 23. Tough central defender who joined Atletico with Molina from Albacete last season and quickly became an ever-present in the side.
Roberto Solozabal, defender, 27. Quiet but influential, Solozabal is the unofficial leader of the Atletico defence and an automatic first-choice.
Toni Munoz, defender, 29. Toni's speed down the left and powerful shot are crucial elements in Atletico's counter-attacking strategy.
Daniel Prodan, defender, 25. Signed over the new year after impressing Radomir Antic with his Champions' League performances for Steaua Bucharest, and scored on his league debut.
Juan Lopez, defender/midfielder, 27. Spanish international utility man who has hardly played this season. A sometimes reckless tackler, Lopez is prone to getting sent off.
Diego Simeone, midfielder, 27. Tough and at times violent midfield dynamo who will only play if he can adequately juggle his responsibilities with the Argentine national side.
Veljko Paunovic, midfielder, 20. Another Yugoslav who has caught the eye of Radomir Antic. Scored on his league debut against Zaragoza last week.
Carlos Aguilera, defender/midfielder, 28. Struggling to hold down a first-team place since rejoining Atletico from Tenerife, Aguilera is strong in joining attacks down the right.
Juan Vizcaino, midfielder, 31. Solid midfielder who provides support for creative chiefs Caminero and Pantic. Has clashed with coach Antic this season after refusing to play out of position.

Milinko Pantic, midfielder, 31. Serbian set-piece specialist who caused a sensation after signing as an unknown from Greek side Panionios last season. Suffers from too many 'off days', and has had a poor season.
Radek Bejbl, midfielder, 24. A star in the Czech Republic's Euro 96 campaign, Bejbl has had a patchy season since signing for Atletico but is likely to start the game in the absence of Simeone.
Roberto Fresnedoso, midfielder, 24. Has improved dramatically this season while filling in for Caminero. Like Santi Denia is currently combining soccer with military service in the army.

Jose Luis Caminero, midfielder, 29. Atletico's undisputed playmaker who shot to prominence in the 1994 World Cup. Caminero has been plagued by injury problems this season, but is keen to win his first derby game against his old club.

Kiko Narvaez, striker, 25. One of the most imaginative strikers in the country, Kiko led Spain to Olympic glory in 1992. Not a great goalscorer, but tends to find the mark at crucial moments. Eager for victory after four years at Atletico without a derby triumph.
Juan Eduardo Esnaider, striker, 24. Argentine who helped Zaragoza to the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1995. Has missed a series of crucial chances this season and is dogged by a vicious temper.
Leonardo Biagini, striker, 20. Promising young Argentine who is only likely to get his chance if Esnaider and Kiko fail.
